plans.note: Section 9 is the express limitation of liability; check mutuality, cap amount/formula (likely tied to fees paid) and carve-outs, and confirm the indemnity in sec-8-2 and warranty disclaimer in sec-8 are excluded from or interact correctly with the cap.

Section 8 (INDEMNIFICATION) should carry Commerce One's third-party IP indemnity in our favour as licensee/host; verify scope, defence/control, exclusions and that any Corio-side indemnity stays narrow.

Field-of-use/market restrictions are most likely in the grant of rights (sec-3) read with the defined terms CORIO MARKET SEGMENT and TERRITORY in sec-1; check for any covenant limiting the applications Corio may host or build.
Look for exclusive-sourcing or exclusive-ASP language in the grant of rights and in Exhibit D (sales and marketing cooperation); confirm Corio remains free to license competing procurement software.
Check the pricing exhibit and fee section for any most-favoured-customer language; an MFN running to Commerce One would be a deviation, one in Corio's favour is acceptable. May well be absent.

No dedicated hiring clause in the outline; if present it would sit in Miscellaneous (sec-14) or alongside the confidentiality/employee NDA provisions (sec-10, EMPLOYEE NDA/INVENTION AGREEMENT definition).
Section 11 governs term and termination; verify whether Corio has termination for convenience on notice and whether Commerce One has any unilateral mid-term exit or termination-fee penalty.
Initial term, renewal mechanics and non-renewal notice window sit in sec-11; cross-check the pricing exhibit for any renewal-term uplift.
Governing law, venue and any arbitration reference (note the defined term RULES) should be in Miscellaneous; California is an accepted law, so check venue/arbitration forum rather than choice of law.

Assignment and change-of-control language is standard in sec-14; confirm Corio may assign to affiliates and successors and that Commerce One cannot terminate on our change of control (particularly a competitor-acquirer trigger).

Ownership allocation likely appears in the grant of rights and the DEVELOPMENTS definition; verify Corio retains its own IP, customer data and any Corio-created developments, and check the trademark and escrow sections for reach-through claims.

Section 2 (GRANT OF RIGHTS, id sec-3) with Exhibit A software list defines scope; check that the licence is non-revocable during term, covers Corio affiliates, contractors and hosted Customers/Software Users, and that Demonstration Software terms are workable.
Given revenue-sharing fees, expect a records/audit right over Corio's reporting in the fees section or Exhibit B payment terms; check frequency, notice, location and who bears cost.
Screen the fee/payment terms for late-payment interest or penalty amounts and termination for any liquidated damages payable by Corio; likely nothing beyond ordinary interest.

Section 7 (WARRANTIES AND DISCLAIMER, id sec-8) with the Warranty Period and Acceptance Test definitions; assess duration, the repair/replace/refund remedy and the breadth of the disclaimer, plus maintenance obligations in sec-5.
No insurance heading in the outline; if any coverage obligation exists it would be buried in Miscellaneous or near the indemnity. Expect to raise as missing.
Exhibit B pricing and revenue-sharing fees are the likely home of any minimum guarantee, committed user count or take-or-pay; check whether shortfalls are payable and whether Corio has an exit.
Effects-of-termination provisions in sec-11 plus the source code escrow in sec-12; verify wind-down rights for hosted Customers, data return and any continuing licence or migration assistance.
